To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypoxia modulates LPS induced TN Falpha expression in murine peritoneal macrophages by enhancing the p38 MAPK activity and that this effect is mediated by HIF 1 alpha induction.
hypoxia modulates the expression of TNF alpha in macrophages by enhancing the activation of p38 MAP kinase and consequently increasing the expression of the downstream effector p MK2.
p38 MAPK inhibition does not affect TNF alpha expression and serum levels during endotoxemia in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate p38 mediated TNFs expression in macrophages and the effect of hypoxic conditions in vivo.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of the immune system in the presence of hypoxia and the role that hypoxia plays in the pathophysiology of sepsis.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the inflammatory response in sepsis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia modulates the p38 MAPKinases signaling pathway and TNF alpha production in LPS induced macrophages.
hypoxia enhances p38 mediated TN Falpha expression in macrophages and that this may be relevant in the context of septic shock and sepsis.
p38 MAPK inhibition by SB203580 in hypoxia conditions did not affect TNF-alpha secretion, suggesting a possible mechanism of resistance to p38 MAPK inhibitors during sepsis and hypoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia modulates the p38 MAPK pathway in macrophages and this modulation is important for TNF alpha expression.
hypoxia modulates p38 MAPK mediated TNF alpha production by increasing MK2 expression and that this effect is relevant in vivo.
hypoxia modulates the p38 MAPK mediated TNF alpha secretion and the effect of SB203580, an inhibitor of p38, on TNF alpha expression is hypoxia dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia is an important factor in the pathogenesis of sepsis and that the p38 MAPK signaling pathway may be a potential therapeutic target in septic patients.

the hypoxic environment in the septic patient may contribute to the increased TNF alpha production and the severity of sepsis and that the p38 MAPK pathway could be an important target for therapeutic intervention.
